competitive_landscape: Today the Lycian coast moves overwhelmingly by road — long, winding coach and taxi transfers on the D400 — supplemented by conventional gulet day-boats and small fixed-schedule ferries (e.g. Meis Express on Kaş↔Kastellorizo). The water between the resort bays is the obvious highway, scenic and congestion-free, yet there is no premium, on-demand, or foiling transfer option. That gap, against a backdrop of 17M+ annual arrivals, is the opportunity.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The dense eastern bay transfers — Antalya↔Kemer (~12 nm), Antalya↔Belek/Side (~20–30 nm), Kaş↔Kekova and Kaş↔Kastellorizo (~2–12 nm) — all sit comfortably inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope with margin for multiple daily rotations.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: The full Lycian line-haul Antalya↔Kaş/Kalkan (>70 nm by sea) is a Quanta-LR hybrid corridor — and because much of the coast between is undeveloped, the hybrid's diesel-refuel removes any dependence on charging infrastructure along the route.

precedents.what: $100M, ~100-vessel electric-hydrofoil network with JIH Global, phased over 3 years (first 5 vessels in 2026)
precedents.why_it_matters: Proof that an all-electric foiling network can be financed and deployed at national scale across a tourism-driven archipelago — the playbook to replicate on a resort coast.

regulatory_note: Turkey is Navier's factory market, making Antalya a strategically valuable domestic deployment with home classification via Türk Loydu. Cross-border micro-hops (Kaş↔Kastellorizo) run through established Turkish/Greek CIQ ports. Marina partners (D-Marin Kemer, Setur Kaş/Finike) operate clean-marina/Blue Flag regimes that align with an all-electric fleet.
seasonality: The Mediterranean coast enjoys a long, calm season (Apr–Oct). Summer afternoons can bring a freshening onshore breeze and short chop in the open bays; foiling rides above that chop for a smoother, more reliable transfer than a planing day-boat. Winter (Nov–Mar) brings occasional storms when service tightens to settled windows.

signature_routes.label: Antalya ↔ Kaş / Kalkan — Lycian line-haul (Quanta-LR hybrid)

summary: Antalya is Turkey's number-one tourism region and one of the busiest leisure gateways on earth, yet its glittering string of resort bays — Kemer, Belek, Side, Kaş, Kalkan — is stitched together by a slow, switch-backed coastal highway and a fleet of conventional gulet day-boats. The water is right there: it is the natural, scenic, congestion-free highway between every one of these destinations, and today it is almost entirely unused for transfers. Antalya is also strategically central to Navier — Turkey is the factory market, so a domestic Lycian-coast network is a home-turf flagship.
tagline: 17 million holidaymakers a year land in Antalya — then crawl for hours along a winding coast road to reach the sea they came for.
